gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-takri: Graceful and stencil-cut, Bevellier packs its flat single-weight strokes tightly, while Noto Sans Takri opens every small round letter wide. Dense on top, breezy below.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Bevellier's strokes look pulled like solder through a nozzle, flat and tightly spaced with squat ascenders. Noto Sans Tamil is a plain sans that looks magnified, so shrinking the heading would blur that gap.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tamil-supp: Sophisticated and unmodulated, Bevellier keeps stems and joins identical in its stencil-cut display letters. And Noto Sans Tamil Supplement answers with round forms like open parentheses and a stocky middle band.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Bevellier is a stencil-cut display face with tight sidebearings and a y whose tail matches its arm. Noto Sans Tangsa, a neutral sans-serif, gives round letters wide openings and short ascender stems, so extended paragraphs feel approachable.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tc: Flat, tight, stencil-sharp. Bevellier outlines every letter with one steady thickness, which earns its keep when big and brief, while Noto Sans TC, a sans-serif, lets its curves open outward.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Diagonals as thick as the horizontals give Bevellier its flat, stencil-cut look, with squat ascenders over a wide-looking lowercase. Noto Sans Thaana, a sans-serif, brings wide channels into big open counters, and that loosening against the tight heading is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-thai: Ruler-straight and tightly packed, Bevellier looks stencil-cut from edge to edge. Noto Sans Thai supplies the strongest single quality here: a swollen, bead-like lowercase with rounded letters left open.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-thai-loope: Noto Sans Thai Looped reads tall and bold-looking, with spacious gaps where its curves end. And Bevellier's wire-weight strokes sit tight above it, so a long passage moves along steadily.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Graceful Bevellier cuts its letters flat from unmodulated strokes, with a wide-looking lowercase and squat ascenders. And Noto Sans Tifinagh fills its lines with open, inflated bowls, so a longer stretch reads softly.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Sharp, flat, stencil-cut. Bevellier holds stems and connecting strokes at one weight and crowds its letters, while Noto Sans Tirhuta answers with a dominant x-height and terminals cut back to leave big gaps.
